1:
Would I go on a last-chance tour? Although seeing a glacier before it disappears sounds exciting, I would not join such a tour.

First of all, tourists who fly to distant places to watch nature vanish are actually speeding up its destruction. Every long flight releases tons of carbon dioxide, which warms the planet and melts the very ice the visitors came to admire. Moreover, crowds of tourists damage fragile areas by leaving rubbish behind and wearing away the paths.

Instead, I would rather learn about endangered places through documentaries and support the organizations that protect them. If more people made this choice, these wonders might survive for future generations.

In conclusion, a last-chance tour may be unforgettable, but it is not worth the price our planet pays.

I think I want to go on a last chance tour. Because I like to see glaciers and mountains. It is very beautiful and I never see it before. My friend go to Iceland last year and he say it was very nice, the ice is big and blue and he take many pictures. Last summer me and my family was in Eilat and we swim in the sea, it was very hot. I think it is good to see the nature before it is gone. But maybe the planes is bad for the enviroment. In the end I want to go becuase it is a last chance.
